quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. You see children playing nearby. What should you do before you move your car?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When backing up, look out your back window for people and obstacles. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially with children nearby. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After a school bus stops with its lights flashing, watch for children walking along the roadside. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: How can you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires work less effectively.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires work less effectively.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less your tires grip the surface. At high speeds, tires lose contact with the road and you may hydroplane (slide on water).

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do?

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.
Do not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk or on overcast days. Use low beam when within 1,000 feet of an approaching vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead fits only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that an upcoming bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on green light must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on green light must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with traffic signals to tell drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. Wait for oncoming traffic to pass.

questions.question: What can help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use signals or your horn when needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid crashes.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
Protecting yourself against bad drivers by passing them in traffic.
Following the car in front of you very closely.
Quickly switching lanes to move around traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you stay safe around reckless, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are in traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross fully without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest driving season.
You should check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
It is safe to use cruise control in winter weather.
Snow tires are best for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use cruise control in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter requires extra caution. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross them to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake firmly. Pull over safely and turn off the engine.

questions.question: Driving while distracted usually:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Slows your reaction time to hazards.
Makes you drive faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow how quickly you react to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: Two drivers reach an open intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to signal they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If you reach an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, yield to that vehicle. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects your stopping ability. Slow down on poor roads to keep control. Driving too fast on slippery roads puts you at risk.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis results from:

options.text: Staring straight ahead at the road for a long time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep before your trip.
Short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring straight ahead at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and stop scanning ahead, behind, and around your vehicle. This causes you to zone out and may cause you to crash into traffic slowing or stopping ahead.

questions.question: You don't have to stop for a flashing school bus if it is on a private road.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and a stop arm out. This rule applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder whenever you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: You should drive with extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means drivers should be prepared to change lanes or let other traffic merge into their lane.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign shows that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one. Be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge in.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Stay out of these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars.

questions.question: Which of the following helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows in the lanes show which lanes to use for different purposes, like going straight or turning.
